root_cause.text: The ADXL380 IIO interrupt handler assumed the FIFO status count was always divisible by the number of enabled scan elements, but the sensor actually produces FIFO entries one sample at a time, so the driver could calculate a batch size larger than the number of entries really present and over-read the FIFO in `adxl380_irq_handler()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `fifo_entries = rounddown(fifo_entries, st->fifo_set_size);` immediately before the loop that does `regmap_noinc_read()` in `adxl380_irq_handler()`, and the commit message explicitly says the FIFO status registers “may not be a multiple of N” and that without rounding down “the number of entries read from the FIFO may exceed the number of entries actually present.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Clamp FIFO entry processing to complete set-sized chunks before reading data from the device FIFO.
intent_record.what: A new statement was inserted in adxl380_irq_handler() to round fifo_entries down to the nearest multiple of st->fifo_set_size before entering the FIFO processing loop.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the handler now avoids iterating over a partial FIFO block by truncating the entry count to a whole number of set-sized chunks, preventing out-of-bounds or inconsistent reads from the FIFO buffer.

grouping_result.intent: Clamp FIFO entry processing to complete set-sized chunks before reading data from the device FIFO.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the reported bug: it clamps FIFO processing to complete scan-sized chunks, preventing the interrupt handler from calculating a batch size larger than the number of actual FIFO entries and over-reading the FIFO.

candidates.rationale: This loop assumes fifo_entries can be consumed in fixed-size chunks of st->fifo_set_size. If the FIFO count is not actually divisible by the number of enabled scan elements, the loop can advance using a batch size larger than the available entries and trigger an over-read in the interrupt handler.

This read pulls a whole batch from the FIFO after the loop has decided how many entries to consume. When the batch size is miscomputed from fifo_entries, this is the operation that can over-read beyond what is actually present in the device FIFO.

vuln_statements.explanation: This loop consumes FIFO data in fixed-size chunks based on st->fifo_set_size, but the sensor produces FIFO entries one sample at a time. If fifo_entries is not truly divisible by the enabled scan elements, the loop can advance as if more complete samples exist than actually do, leading to an over-read in the interrupt handler.

This read fetches a full batch from the FIFO after the loop decides how many entries to consume. Because the batch size can be miscomputed from fifo_entries under the faulty assumption of divisibility, this operation can over-read beyond the data actually present in the FIFO.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable interrupt-handler logic is present and matches the root cause. In `adxl380_irq_handler()` the driver reads the FIFO entry count with `adxl380_get_fifo_entries(st, &fifo_entries);` and then iterates `for (i = 0; i < fifo_entries; i += st->fifo_set_size) { ... regmap_noinc_read(..., 2 * st->fifo_set_size); ... }`. This assumes the FIFO count is directly consumable in batches of `st->fifo_set_size`, but there is no check that `fifo_entries` is an exact multiple of `st->fifo_set_size`, nor any clamping of the final read size. Since the function reads `2 * st->fifo_set_size` bytes per iteration from `ADXL380_FIFO_DATA`, this can over-read if the sensor provides fewer entries than the batch size implies. The fix is not present here; there is no handling like taking the minimum of remaining entries and batch size or otherwise ensuring the FIFO count aligns with the scan size.
